question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $2<4x-3<3$ or $4x-3\ge 4.$
question.worked_solution:
We start by solving $2<4x-3<3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & <4x-3<3 \\ 5 & <4x<6 \\ \frac{5}{4} & <x<\frac{6}{4} \\ \frac{5}{4} & <x<\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/bac195a89ad5d09fa7753fe32bc5f4633453d37816c53330321e000579a8cb85.png)

Then, we solve $4x-3\ge 4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3 & \ge 4 \\ 4x & \ge 7 \\ x & \ge \frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/09fd2be8420b15d39149183d5b802fdcdbd20739ab7364663e0592e61aaf12df.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/6ac5a412c535841b9872b1cbe4edee815e173dd43f3bb757616b7ca9a68200b8.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $\frac{5}{4}<x<\frac{3}{2}$ or $x\ge \frac{7}{4}.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(\frac{5}{4},\frac{3}{2})\cup [\frac{7}{4},\infty ).
$$
